what.text: Sildenafil is a small-molecule drug called a PDE5 inhibitor. It is the active ingredient in Viagra, approved for erectile dysfunction (ED), and in Revatio, approved for pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH), which is high blood pressure in the arteries of the lungs.
How it acts, according to the FDA label

items.text: During sexual stimulation, nerves and blood-vessel cells in the penis release nitric oxide. Nitric oxide raises a messenger called cGMP, which relaxes smooth muscle and lets blood flow in.
The enzyme PDE5 breaks cGMP down. Sildenafil blocks PDE5, so cGMP stays higher. The label says it has no effect without sexual stimulation.
Sildenafil and its main breakdown product each have a half-life of about 4 hours.

research.text: Sildenafil has a large body of randomized trials. The Viagra label describes 21 randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials of up to 6 months in more than 3,000 men aged 19 to 87. Two published trials, and one study of sildenafil taken alongside tadalafil, are listed below as they were run.

The label trials used several designs (fixed dose, dose titration, parallel and crossover) in men with ED of physical, psychological or mixed causes. The main measure was a questionnaire, the International Index of Erectile Function (IIEF).

research.title: Erectile dysfunction, two trials (NEJM 1998)

facts.v: Goldstein I, Lue TF, Padma-Nathan H, et al. N Engl J Med 1998;338(20):1397-404
two sequential double-blind, placebo-controlled studies, then an open-label extension
532 men in a dose-response study; 329 different men in a flexible-dose study, of whom 225 entered the extension. ED of physical, psychological and mixed causes.
sildenafil 25, 50 or 100 mg or placebo, as needed (dose-response study); sildenafil or placebo with dose increases up to 100 mg (flexible-dose study)
IIEF questionnaire, a patient log and a global question

research.found: In the last 4 weeks of the flexible-dose study, 69% of attempts at intercourse were successful on sildenafil and 22% on placebo (P<0.001). Headache, flushing and indigestion were the most common side effects, in 6% to 18% of men. 92% of men completed the extension.

research.title: Pulmonary arterial hypertension, SUPER-1 (NEJM 2005)

facts.v: Galiè N, Ghofrani HA, Torbicki A, et al. N Engl J Med 2005;353(20):2148-57
278 people with symptomatic PAH (idiopathic, linked to connective-tissue disease, or after repaired congenital heart shunts)
sildenafil 20, 40 or 80 mg or placebo, three times a day
12 weeks, with an optional long-term extension
change in 6-minute walk distance (main measure); lung artery pressure, WHO functional class and clinical worsening

research.found: Compared with placebo, walk distance rose by 45 m, 46 m and 50 m in the three dose groups (P<0.001 for each). Clinical worsening did not differ significantly from placebo. Flushing, indigestion and diarrhea were reported. The study was not powered to assess deaths.

research.title: Daily tadalafil with or without sildenafil as needed (Andrologia 2015)

facts.v: Cui H, Liu B, Song Z, et al. Andrologia 2015;47(1):20-4
two groups assigned 1:1. The abstract does not say whether the study was blinded or placebo-controlled.
tadalafil 5 mg once daily alone, or tadalafil 5 mg once daily plus sildenafil 50 mg as needed
IIEF-5 questionnaire, Sexual Encounter Profile, side effects

research.found: IIEF-5 scores were higher in the combined group among men with severe ED. Side-effect rates did not differ between groups. The two drugs were given on separate schedules; this was not a study of a single combined product.

research.text: A PubMed search found no published human study of sildenafil given as a gum, gummy, troche or oral strip, or combined with oxytocin.
In extracts of smooth-muscle cells from human penile tissue (corpus cavernosum), sildenafil blocked PDE5 and raised cGMP in intact cells when a nitric oxide donor was added. This was a cell study.

us.text: Sildenafil is FDA approved, by prescription, as Viagra (1998, ED), Revatio (2005, PAH) and Vybrique oral film (2025, ED). Compounded versions are not FDA approved. As of October 31, 2026.

items.text: approved March 27, 1998 (NDA 020895) as a new molecular entity, with priority review. Approved use: treatment of erectile dysfunction.

tablets approved June 3, 2005 (NDA 021845); an intravenous solution approved November 18, 2009 (NDA 022473). Approved use: PAH (WHO Group I) in adults, to improve exercise ability and delay clinical worsening, and in children aged 1 to 17.
a sildenafil oral film placed on the tongue, approved December 16, 2025 (NDA 210858) for erectile dysfunction. Compounded sildenafil strips are a different, unapproved product.
the label says sildenafil must not be used with nitrates or nitric oxide donors in any form, or with guanylate cyclase stimulators such as riociguat.
the Viagra label says combinations with other PDE5 inhibitors, including Revatio, or with other ED treatments have not been studied, may further lower blood pressure, and are not recommended.
FDA's Drugs@FDA data list no approved product that combines sildenafil with tadalafil.

items.text: taking sildenafil as a gum, gummy or troche, or in one dose with tadalafil or oxytocin, is not an approved use. It is off-label.

us.text: Compounded sildenafil gums, gummies, troches and oral strips, including combinations with tadalafil or oxytocin, are not FDA approved.
FDA says compounded drugs are not FDA approved, which means FDA does not verify their safety, effectiveness or quality before they are marketed.

world.lead: Sildenafil is an approved prescription medicine in the US, the EU and Australia. In the UK, one 50 mg brand, Viagra Connect, may be sold by pharmacists without a prescription. Canada's status was not confirmed. It is not on WADA's Prohibited List.

countries.status: Approved medicine (Viagra 1998, ED; Revatio 2005, PAH; Vybrique oral film 2025, ED). Prescription-only.
Status being confirmed with the regulator's record.

Viagra Connect (sildenafil 50 mg) reclassified from prescription-only to pharmacy medicine in November 2017, for men over 18 with ED, sold after a talk with a pharmacist. MHRA says pharmacy sales began in 2018.
Approved medicine. Viagra authorised September 13, 1998 (ED); Revatio authorised October 28, 2005 (PAH). Prescription-only.
Approved medicine: TGA publishes product information for Viagra, Revatio and other sildenafil brands. Prescription-only (Schedule 4).

after.text: Canada: in January 2026, Health Canada warned about counterfeit Viagra and Cialis seized in Ontario. It described sildenafil and tadalafil as prescription drugs that should be used only under a health care professional's supervision and never with nitrate drugs.

after.title: Sport
after.text: Sildenafil is not named on the WADA 2026 Prohibited List or on the 2027 List, which takes effect January 1, 2027. It is not in the 2027 Monitoring Program either. Class S0 covers only substances with no government approval for human use, and sildenafil is approved (see above).

side.text: The label lists headache, flushing and indigestion as the most common side effects. Serious risks include a dangerous drop in blood pressure with nitrates, erections lasting more than 4 hours, sudden vision loss and sudden hearing loss.

items.lead: Common, in the label's fixed-dose trials:
items.text: headache (16% to 28% on sildenafil vs 7% on placebo), flushing (10% to 19% vs 2%), indigestion (3% to 17% vs 2%), abnormal vision (1% to 11% vs 1%, mostly a color tinge, light sensitivity or blurring), stuffy nose, back pain, muscle pain, nausea, dizziness and rash. Some rose with dose. 2.5% stopped for side effects, vs 2.3% on placebo.
contraindicated. Sildenafil was shown to strengthen the blood-pressure-lowering effect of nitrates.

ED treatments should not generally be used in men for whom sexual activity is inadvisable because of their heart condition. In healthy volunteers, blood pressure fell by a mean maximum of 8.4/5.5 mmHg. There are no controlled data in men who had a heart attack, stroke or life-threatening arrhythmia in the last 6 months, men with resting blood pressure below 90/50 or above 170/110, or men with heart failure or unstable angina.
erections over 4 hours and priapism (painful erections over 6 hours) have been reported infrequently. Untreated priapism can damage penile tissue and cause permanent loss of potency.
sudden loss of vision in one or both eyes can be a sign of NAION, a type of optic nerve damage. The label tells patients to stop and seek care.
sudden decrease or loss of hearing, sometimes with ringing in the ears and dizziness, has been reported in time with PDE5 inhibitor use. It is not known whether the drug caused it.

items.lead: Low blood pressure with other drugs:
items.text: caution with alpha-blockers and blood-pressure medicines. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors such as ritonavir raise sildenafil levels.
the Viagra label says combining it with other PDE5 inhibitors has not been studied, may lower blood pressure further, and is not recommended.
use in pulmonary veno-occlusive disease may cause fluid in the lungs; in pulmonary hypertension from sickle cell disease it may cause serious vaso-occlusive crises.

in 2018 MHRA reported that a Dutch trial of sildenafil for fetal growth restriction was stopped early: 17 of 64 babies (27%) in the sildenafil group had persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn, including 11 deaths before discharge, vs 3 of 58 (5%) and no deaths on placebo. Sildenafil is not authorised for this use.

MHRA seized about 19.5 million doses of illegally traded ED medicines from 2021 to 2025, including sildenafil. It says such products may contain no active ingredient, the wrong dose, hidden drugs or toxic ingredients.

unconfirmed: Health Canada's Drug Product Database could not be reached, so no Canadian authorization of Viagra, Revatio or another sildenafil brand is confirmed here.
TGA's ARTG (tga.gov.au) did not respond; Australian status rests on TGA's PI/CMI search and the Poisons Standard.
The year FDA approved Revatio for children aged 1 to 17 was not confirmed.
No published human study of sildenafil as a gum, gummy, troche or oral strip, or with oxytocin, was found; this rests on one PubMed search.
surprises: Viagra Connect is often dated to 2017: MHRA announced the reclassification in November 2017 ('if marketed'), and MHRA later said pharmacy sales began in 2018.
